question.prompt: Centers of adjacent faces of a unit cube are joined to form a regular octahedron. What is the volume of this octahedron?

solutions.explanation:
The four centers of the cube's vertical faces lie halfway between its top and bottom faces. They form a square that divides the octahedron into two square pyramids, whose tips are the top and bottom face centers.

In this middle plane, the four centers are the side midpoints of a unit square. Their square has two perpendicular diagonals of length \(1\). Splitting along one diagonal gives two triangles, each with base \(1\) and height \(\tfrac12\). Thus the common base area is
\[
B=2\left(\frac12\cdot1\cdot\frac12\right)=\frac12.
\]
Each pyramid has perpendicular height \(h=\tfrac12\). Using the pyramid volume formula \(V=\tfrac13 Bh\), the octahedron's volume is
\[
2\left(\frac13\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12\right)=\boxed{\frac16}.
\]
The answer is choice B.
solutions.title: Split into two square pyramids
